answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a vault as the anchor of the cost. A island stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a marble hold...
